meta.title: One Run, End to End

views.label: 1 · You start it
views.note: You call run() with a plan and ports. Started and Composed come back at once — you read the run as it happens, not after.

views.label: 2 · The step asks first
views.note: Every step is judged on its effect profile before the component is called. There is no path around this.

views.label: 3 · The agent thinks
views.note: The agent is a component like any other. It calls the model; the runtime never talks to a model itself.

views.label: 4 · When it must ask you
views.note: Ask parks the run on a checkpoint. You answer whenever you like, even from a different process.

views.label: 5 · What is kept
views.note: A proposal asks you to remember something. Ended closes the stream with one of five named reasons.

meta.subtitle: Who calls whom, in what order, from your first call to the last event.

messages.label: Asked — the run parks on a checkpoint

cards.title: Who each lifeline is
items: Host — your product. It starts the run and reads the events
run() — the loop. It drives the graph and owns the event stream
Governed step — the seven moves; every node of the compiled graph is one of these
Governance — your policy. Shown effects and context, it answers Allow, Ask or Refuse
Agent — an ordinary component that happens to be the one which calls a model
Model — whatever thinks. Any provider, behind one adapter
Sink — where a proposal lands. Your gate decides whether it becomes truth

cards.title: Reading the arrows
items: A solid arrow is a call: someone is waiting for the answer
A thin return arrow is the answer coming back
A dashed arrow is information, not a request — nobody waits for it
A red arrow is a governance decision or a security-relevant answer
The bands down the left are the acts of the run; use the chapters above to step through them

cards.title: Nothing runs unjudged
items: Governance is asked before the component is called, and a Refuse means it is never called at all
It is shown the effect profile and the context — never the component's name or your product's meaning
Ask parks the run; Allow and Refuse settle it on the spot

cards.title: Two different exits
items: A component changes the world and returns an observation the agent can see
A proposal goes to the sink, and you alone decide whether it becomes truth
The runtime has no write path into any durable store
